gap: No result ChatGPT got names or prices a single power bank. Today the largest bank that needs no airline approval sells for $79.99 to $249.95 on makers' stores. The 99.36 Wh AOHi Future Starship is $119, and EcoFlow's 99.54 Wh RAPID Pro is $154.99. That is $36 more for 0.18 Wh more.
standout_why: I read the eCFR copy of 49 CFR 175.10 (law.cornell.edu), which ChatGPT got but did not cite. It gives the rule: 100 Wh, up to two spares of 101–160 Wh with operator approval, spares in carry-on only. It names no products or prices. The FAA PackSafe pages and the cited American Airlines restricted-items page returned HTTP 403 to WebFetch. The cited IATA power-bank PDF downloaded, but WebFetch could not decode its text, and the local text-extraction commands were blocked (they needed approval). So I could not check those pages' wording. Their titles and ChatGPT's own answer show they are rule pages, and ChatGPT showed no catalog cards. A priced list of models at the 99–100 Wh ceiling and in the approval-required band is new.
decides: This confirms the AOHi Future Starship 240W ($119, 99.36 Wh) as the pick for the biggest no-approval bank. It matches the EcoFlow RAPID Pro within 0.2 Wh for $35.99 less. Our page's EcoFlow price is stale: it is $154.99 today, not $175.99. The 40,000 mAh AOHi Starship ($179) is the only listed model in the 101–160 Wh band. eCFR says that band needs operator approval, and ChatGPT's answer says American Airlines now caps power banks at 100 Wh, so it suits only shoppers who confirm their airline allows it. For less money with slightly less capacity, UGREEN's 145W 25,000 mAh (90 Wh) and AOHi's Black Warrior (90.72 Wh) are both $79.99.

findings.label: US spare-battery limit (49 CFR 175.10(a)(18))
findings.value: ≤100 Wh with no approval; with operator approval, up to 2 spares of >100–160 Wh per person; spares in carry-on only
findings.source_title: 49 CFR § 175.10 - Exceptions for passengers, crewmembers, and air operators (LII)
findings.note: Quoted text: 'no more than two individually protected lithium ion batteries each exceeding 100 Wh, but not exceeding 160 Wh, may be carried per person as spare batteries in carry-on baggage'
